## Details
### **SW-REQ-MLOG-001** — Raw IMU Record API

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept raw IMU sample records and write them to non-volatile storage.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-001 and SW-REQ-SYS-022, raw IMU samples must be persisted to the SD card for post-flight analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-022
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-002** — Raw Barometer Record API

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept raw barometer sample records and write them to non-volatile storage.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-001 and SW-REQ-SYS-022, raw barometer samples must be persisted to the SD card.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-022
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-003** — Raw GPS NMEA Record API

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept raw GPS NMEA sentences and write them verbatim to non-volatile storage.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-024, raw GPS NMEA sentences must be preserved verbatim for post-flight reconstruction.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-024
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-004** — Navigation State Record API

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept navigation state records and write them to non-volatile storage.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-022, navigation state estimates must be persisted to the SD card for post-flight analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-022
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-005** — AFM Phase Event Record API

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept flight phase event records and write them to non-volatile storage.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-022, AFM flight phase events must be persisted to the SD card for post-flight analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-022
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-006** — GPS UTC Time Record API

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept GPS UTC time records and write them to non-volatile storage.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-028, GPS UTC time records enable post-flight alignment of monotonic time to absolute UTC.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-028
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-007** — Per-Record Monotonic Microsecond Timestamp

- **Description:** The mlog library shall stamp every written record with a monotonic microsecond timestamp.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-026 and SW-REQ-SYS-027, every record (including per-sample raw records) must carry a monotonic microsecond stamp.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-026
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-008** — New Run Created at Initialization

- **Description:** The mlog library shall create a new log run on each initialization.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-025, each power-on must start a fresh log run distinct from prior runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-025
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-009** — Prior Run Preservation

- **Description:** The mlog library shall not overwrite or delete any prior log run.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-055, prior log runs must be preserved on the SD card until externally wiped.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-055
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-010** — Machine-Parseable Record Format

- **Description:** The mlog library shall write records in a machine-parseable format that identifies each record's type.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-023, log records must be machine-parseable; specific format details are deferred to design.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-023
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-011** — Write Failure Status Propagation

- **Description:** The mlog library shall return a failure status to the caller when the underlying SD write fails.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-035 and SW-REQ-SYS-060, SD write failures must be observable so callers can flag the SD unhealthy and continue.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-060
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-012** — Continue After Write Failure

- **Description:** The mlog library shall accept and attempt subsequent record writes after a prior write failure.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-035, the FSW must continue attempting SD writes after a write failure rather than halting.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-035
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-013** — POSIX and Pico2 Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The mlog library shall provide functionally equivalent behavior on the POSIX and Pico2 builds.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-043, the POSIX build must be functionally equivalent to the Pico2 flight build for Trick simulation.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-014** — Deterministic Record Output

- **Description:** The mlog library shall produce identical written record byte sequences given identical input record sequences.
- **Rationale:** Per SW-REQ-SYS-044, deterministic output is required for repeatable Trick simulation runs and regression analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-TC-MLOG-001** — Raw IMU Record Write - Round Trip

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-MLOG-001, SW-REQ-MLOG-010
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Initialize mlog library against a tmpfs/in-memory storage backend with a fresh run.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Write API returns success and the parsed IMU record exactly matches the input accelerometer and gyroscope values, with the record type identifying it as an IMU record.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Construct a raw IMU sample record with known accelerometer and gyroscope values.
  2. Call the mlog write API for IMU records with the constructed sample.
  3. Close or flush the run to ensure bytes are durable.
  4. Re-open the produced log file and parse records using the documented format.
  5. Locate the IMU record and compare every field against the input sample.

## Details
### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-001** — Subscribe to Data-of-Interest Bus Messages

- **Description:** The mlog app shall subscribe to all data-of-interest software bus messages required for SD card logging.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: route all data-of-interest SB messages to mlog_lib for SD card persistence per SW-REQ-SYS-022 and SW-REQ-SYS-024.

- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-022
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-002** — Forward Records at Full Sample Rate

- **Description:** The mlog app shall forward each subscribed message to the mlog library without downsampling.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: persist each sensor sample at its full rate to satisfy raw fidelity logging.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-001
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-003** — Initiate New Log Run on Startup

- **Description:** The mlog app shall initiate a new log run via the mlog library at startup.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: each power-on starts a fresh log run distinct from prior runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-025
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-004** — Preserve Prior Log Runs on Startup

- **Description:** The mlog app shall not delete or overwrite prior log runs when initiating a new run.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: protect prior flight data against accidental overwrite between runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-055
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-005** — Stamp Forwarded Records With Monotonic Microseconds

- **Description:** The mlog app shall stamp each forwarded record with monotonic microseconds since startup.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: every record uses one canonical time source for cross-record alignment.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-026
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-006** — Per-Sample Timestamping

- **Description:** The mlog app shall include a timestamp on every individual sensor sample record forwarded to the library.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: per-sample timestamps required for accurate post-flight nav reconstruction.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-027
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-007** — Forward Verbatim NMEA Sentences

- **Description:** The mlog app shall forward GPS NMEA sentences to the mlog library without modification.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: preserve unmodified GPS source data for post-flight reconstruction.

- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-024
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-008** — Forward GPS UTC Records

- **Description:** The mlog app shall forward each received GPS UTC message to the mlog library.
- **Rationale:** Module purpose: enables post-flight alignment of monotonic time to absolute UTC.

- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-028
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-009** — Continue After SD Write Failure

- **Description:** The mlog app shall continue forwarding subsequent records after the mlog library reports a write failure.

- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-035
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-MLOG-APP-010** — Expose SD Card Health to System Aggregator

- **Description:** The mlog app shall expose SD card write health to sys_app via the sd_lib health query interface.
- **Rationale:** PM Decision 3 (sprint 2026-05-02): SD health observability is delegated to sys_app's IsHealthy() poll model rather than a dedicated bus message; bitmap aggregation lives in sys_app per architecture.

### **SW-TC-MLOG-APP-005** — Stamp Forwarded Records With Monotonic Microseconds

- **Verification Method:** Test

- **Acceptance Criteria:** Captured timestamps equal {1000, 2500, 9000} microseconds (monotonic, non-decreasing, in microsecond units).

  2. Advance the clock to t2 = 9000 us and publish a third bus message.
  3. Drive mlog_app to process the queued messages.
  4. Read the captured timestamps from the fake mlog_lib.

- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-017** — Body Axes Convention for IMU Inputs

- **Description:** The nav library shall treat IMU body-frame inputs as X-forward, Y-right, Z-down.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-057 body axes convention into the nav library input interpretation contract.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-057
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-018** — EKF Filter Algorithm

- **Description:** The nav library shall use an Extended Kalman Filter to estimate the navigation state vector.
- **Rationale:** PM-pinned filter choice (2026-05-03); EKF balances FT1 nonlinear dynamics with kmat-implementable Jacobians and bounded WCET on Pico2.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-013
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-019** — Configurable Noise Covariance Loading

- **Description:** The nav library shall accept caller-supplied noise covariance values via NAV_INIT_T at initialization.
- **Rationale:** PM directive 2026-05-03: all noise/covariance values must be load-time configurable to enable per-build tuning without recompilation; the design provides reference values as installation guidance only.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-NAV-001
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-020** — Configurable Initial State Covariance Loading

- **Description:** The nav library shall accept caller-supplied initial state covariance values via NAV_INIT_T at initialization.
- **Rationale:** Closes implementation-readiness gap G2 from 2026-05-03 SSE-R re-review: P_0 (initial state covariance) governs how quickly the filter trusts measurements relative to the seed; same load-time-configurable philosophy as SW-REQ-NAV-019 (noise covariance) per PM directive 2026-05-03. Without this, two implementers could choose P_0=0 (locks state at seed) or P_0=large (accepts all measurements) producing radically different startup behavior.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-NAV-019
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-TC-NAV-021** — EKF Prediction Step Verification

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-NAV-018
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Initialize NAV_LIB_IMPL_T with deterministic NAV_INIT_T (zero biases, fInitialCovDiag = small values [1e-6 across all 16 entries, expressing high confidence in the seed], kNavGpsBoundM_default, all noise sigmas set to the algorithm.md §5.2 reference values). Inject a known-good IMU_SAMPLE_T sequence (3 samples at 5 ms intervals) covering a small acceleration in body X-axis. Reference EKF script: libs/nav_lib/tests/ekf_reference.py — Python NumPy implementation using the analytic F derived from Groves 2013 §14.2 (the same normative reference the IMPL uses per algorithm.md §3.2 step 8); seeded from the same NAV_INIT_T values; double precision throughout.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Final NAV_STATE position differs from NAV_STATE_REF by less than 1 cm (Euclidean horizontal-position distance after lat/lon-to-meter conversion at the seed latitude); velocity by less than 1 cm/s (Euclidean magnitude over the 3-element NED triple); quaternion components by less than 1e-6 each (per-component absolute difference; quaternion is dimensionless — Euclidean component distance, NOT radians). bValid=true throughout. JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS on every call.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Call `nav_lib::Init()` with the deterministic NAV_INIT_T.
  2. Call `nav_lib::PredictImu(sample0)` and capture the resulting NAV_STATE.
  3. Call `nav_lib::PredictImu(sample1)` and `nav_lib::PredictImu(sample2)` in sequence.
  4. Call `nav_lib::GetState()` and capture the final NAV_STATE.
  5. Run libs/nav_lib/tests/ekf_reference.py with the same NAV_INIT_T and IMU sequence; capture its final NAV_STATE_REF as the ground-truth comparison vector.
  6. Compare position, velocity, and quaternion components element-wise: |NAV_STATE - NAV_STATE_REF|.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - ekf_reference.py (other): Python NumPy reference EKF implementation using analytic F per Groves 2013 §14.2; produces ground-truth NAV_STATE_REF for SW-TC-NAV-021 acceptance comparison
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/nav_lib/tests/nav_lib_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-NAV-022** — NAV_INIT_T Configurable Noise Covariance Loading

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-NAV-019
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Construct two distinct NAV_INIT_T instances with the same biases and bounds but different noise covariance values (e.g., NAV_INIT_T_A with sigma_accel = 1e-3 m/s^2/sqrt(Hz) and sigma_GPS_horiz = 1.0 m; NAV_INIT_T_B with sigma_accel = 1e-2 m/s^2/sqrt(Hz) and sigma_GPS_horiz = 5.0 m). Prepare an identical input sequence (3 IMU samples + 1 GPS update).
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Both invocations return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS. NAV_STATE_A.tPosLla differs from NAV_STATE_B.tPosLla by greater than 0.1 m, demonstrating the covariance values were loaded and used by the filter (not silently discarded). Both NAV_STATE bValid=true.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Initialize a fresh NAV_LIB_IMPL_T_A with NAV_INIT_T_A; feed the input sequence; capture final NAV_STATE_A.
  2. Initialize a fresh NAV_LIB_IMPL_T_B with NAV_INIT_T_B; feed the same input sequence; capture final NAV_STATE_B.
  3. Compare NAV_STATE_A.tPosLla[0..2] vs NAV_STATE_B.tPosLla[0..2]; compute the position-difference magnitude.
  4. Verify that NAV_STATE_A and NAV_STATE_B differ — the higher-noise covariance instance should weight the IMU prediction more strongly relative to the GPS update.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/nav_lib/tests/nav_lib_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-NAV-023** — NAV_INIT_T Configurable Initial State Covariance Loading

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-NAV-020
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Construct two distinct NAV_INIT_T instances with the same biases, bounds, and noise covariances but different initial state covariance diagonals: NAV_INIT_T_LOW with fInitialCovDiag set to small values (e.g., 1e-6 across all 16 states, expressing high confidence in the seed); NAV_INIT_T_HIGH with fInitialCovDiag set to large values (e.g., 1e2 across all 16 states, expressing low confidence). Prepare an identical input sequence (1 IMU sample + 1 GPS update with a position 100 m offset from the NAV_INIT_T.tInitialState seed).
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Both invocations return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS. NAV_STATE_LOW horizontal position is within 10 m of the NAV_INIT_T.tInitialState seed and more than 50 m from the GPS observation. NAV_STATE_HIGH horizontal position is within 10 m of the GPS observation and more than 50 m from the seed. The contrast demonstrates that the fInitialCovDiag values were loaded into P_0 and used by the filter at first measurement update.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Initialize a fresh NAV_LIB_IMPL_T_LOW with NAV_INIT_T_LOW; feed the input sequence; capture final NAV_STATE_LOW.
  2. Initialize a fresh NAV_LIB_IMPL_T_HIGH with NAV_INIT_T_HIGH; feed the same input sequence; capture final NAV_STATE_HIGH.
  3. Compute horizontal-position deviation of NAV_STATE_LOW from the NAV_INIT_T.tInitialState seed and from the GPS observation; same for NAV_STATE_HIGH.
  4. Verify that NAV_STATE_LOW remains close to the seed (high P_0 confidence weights GPS less) and NAV_STATE_HIGH moves close to the GPS observation (low P_0 confidence weights GPS more).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/nav_lib/tests/nav_lib_test.cpp

### **SW-REQ-NAV-APP-010** — Continue Publishing on Missing Inputs

- **Description:** The nav app shall continue publishing navigation state at 100 Hz when one or more sensor inputs are unavailable.
- **Rationale:** Parent SYS-034 requires nav propagation to continue when sensor inputs drop.
- **Verification Method:** Test

- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-034
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-APP-011** — Position Bound to Latest GPS Fix

- **Description:** The nav app shall keep its published position estimate within a configured horizontal distance of the latest GPS fix.
- **Rationale:** Parent SYS-014 mandates a black-box GPS divergence bound at the app boundary.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-014
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-APP-012** — POSIX Build Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The nav app shall produce identical published navigation state on POSIX and Pico2 builds for identical inputs.
- **Rationale:** Parent SYS-043 requires the POSIX build to be functionally equivalent to the Pico2 build.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-APP-013** — Deterministic Navigation Output

- **Description:** The nav app shall produce deterministic navigation state output given identical sensor input sequences.
- **Rationale:** Parent SYS-044 requires deterministic outputs for repeatable Trick sim runs and regression analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-APP-014** — Boost-Phase Sensor Update Skipping

- **Description:** The nav app shall skip baro and GPS measurement updates during the boost phase.
- **Rationale:** PM directive 2026-05-03: GPS multipath and baro shock during boost (high-G, transient pressure) make those measurements unreliable; IMU-only dead-reckoning is the safer fusion strategy during the ~500 ms boost interval.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-013
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NAV-APP-015** — Post-Boost Settling Window for Sensor Re-Enablement

- **Description:** The nav app shall delay baro and GPS update re-enablement by one second after boost-phase exit.
- **Rationale:** PM directive 2026-05-03: 1-second settling window allows IMU bias estimates to converge after the boost-phase shock before fusion of GPS and baro resumes; configurable via NAV_APP_INIT_T for per-build tuning.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-NAV-APP-014
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

- **Setup:** Pico2 flight board powered with GPS, IMU, and barometer connected. Telemetry logger capturing software bus traffic. Outdoor location with clear sky view. Divergence bound configured to mission value.

  4. Stop the run and save the telemetry log to file.
  5. Run the post-processing script to compute, for each nav state, the horizontal distance to the latest GPS fix.

- **Status:** Active

After (t_exit + 1.0 s), stub nav_lib received UpdateBaro and UpdateGps calls on every subsequent tick. PredictImu called on every OnProcess invocation throughout. nav_app returned JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS throughout.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Inject JUNO_MSG_AFM_PHASE_T with ePhase=JUNO_PHASE_BOOST; advance 5 ticks while delivering IMU/baro/GPS samples (no Update calls expected).
  2. Inject JUNO_MSG_AFM_PHASE_T with ePhase=JUNO_PHASE_APOGEE; record the boost-exit time as t_exit.
  3. Advance time by 0.5 seconds (50 x 10 ms ticks); on each tick deliver IMU/baro/GPS samples and call OnProcess. Verify NO UpdateBaro/UpdateGps calls (still inside settling window).
  4. Advance time to (t_exit + 1.001 seconds); call OnProcess; deliver IMU/baro/GPS.
  5. Continue for 3 more ticks; verify UpdateBaro and UpdateGps are now called on every tick.

## Details
### **SW-REQ-NMEA-001** — GGA Sentence Parsing

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall parse GGA sentences into latitude, longitude, altitude, satellite count, and fix quality.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-038 and SW-REQ-SYS-039: GGA is the primary NMEA carrier of WGS-84 geodetic position and altitude. The five fields are bundled into one requirement because the public API ingests one sentence and returns one populated struct in a single observable I/O call; splitting per-field would not reflect a separately observable behavior at the library boundary.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-038
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-002** — RMC Sentence Parsing

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall parse RMC sentences into latitude, longitude, ground speed, course, and UTC time.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-028: RMC carries UTC time and ground-speed/course needed for downstream nav and time alignment. The five fields are bundled into one requirement because the public API ingests one sentence and returns one populated struct in a single observable I/O call; splitting per-field would not reflect a separately observable behavior at the library boundary.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-028
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-003** — Checksum Validation

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall validate the embedded checksum of each NMEA sentence before producing parsed output.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-038: downstream geodetic position consumers require parsed-output integrity, so the checksum is verified on every sentence to prevent corrupted bytes from polluting reported lat/lon/altitude.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-038
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-004** — Reject Sentences with Invalid Checksum

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall return an error status when a sentence checksum does not match.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-038: parsed geodetic position must be trustworthy, so the parser surfaces checksum failures as an error status enabling callers to discard tainted data rather than emit corrupted lat/lon downstream.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-038
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-005** — Decimal Geodetic Coordinate Output

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall convert latitude and longitude from degrees-minutes format to a single geodetic decimal value.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-038: NMEA emits ddmm.mmmm; downstream consumers require a single decimal scalar in WGS-84. This requirement is the unit-conversion contract (degrees-minutes to decimal degrees), distinct from SW-REQ-NMEA-001 which is the field-extraction contract for GGA.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-038
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-006** — Altitude Reported in Meters

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall report parsed altitude in meters.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-039 and SW-REQ-SYS-042: altitude unit must be preserved as meters (SI) for downstream HAE interpretation.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-039
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-007** — Ground Speed Converted to SI Units

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall convert ground speed from knots to meters per second in parsed output.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-042: NMEA RMC reports speed in knots; FSW SI units mandate conversion at the parser boundary.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-042
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-008** — UTC Time Extraction

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall extract UTC time of fix from each parsed sentence containing it.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-028: GPS UTC time logging requires the parser to surface UTC from GGA and RMC.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-028
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-009** — Sentence Type Identification

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall identify the sentence type of each input message before parsing it.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-028: extracting UTC requires discriminating GGA from RMC (and other types) so the parser dispatches sentence-type-specific field extraction before producing UTC output.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-028
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-010** — POSIX and Pico2 Parser Equivalence

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall produce identical parsed outputs on POSIX and Pico2 builds for identical inputs.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-043: as a pure parser the library must be byte-equivalent across both build targets.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-011** — Deterministic Parsing

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall produce deterministic parsed outputs given identical input sentences.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-044: parser determinism is required for repeatable Trick sim and regression analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-NMEA-012** — Reject Malformed Fields

- **Description:** The NMEA library shall return an error status when a sentence field is malformed or out of bounds.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-044: deterministic FSW outputs require the parser to reject non-numeric, oversized, or otherwise malformed fields with an error status rather than silently emit garbage values that would corrupt downstream determinism.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

  2. Run the NMEA Google Test suite on the Pico2 build (or its host-mode equivalent) and write the captured parsed-output bytes to a fixture artifact.
  3. Programmatically byte-compare the two artifacts inside a Google Test that loads both fixtures and asserts equality.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/nmea_lib/tests/nmea_lib_test.cpp

## Details
### **SW-REQ-SCH-001** — Application Registration With Fixed Period

- **Description:** The SCH library shall register applications with a fixed period at startup.
- **Rationale:** PM-mandated static TDM model: every application has a compile-time period set during initialization.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-002** — Static Schedule After Initialization

- **Description:** The SCH library shall reject application registration after scheduler initialization completes.
- **Rationale:** PM decision SW-REQ-SYS-010: schedule is fixed at compile time; no dynamic registration permitted after init.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-003** — Periodic Application Invocation

- **Description:** The SCH library shall invoke each registered application at its registered period.
- **Rationale:** Core TDM behavior: apps run on their fixed cadence so sensor and nav rates are met deterministically.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-004** — Period Range Covers FSW Application Rates

- **Description:** The SCH library shall support application periods spanning at least 5 milliseconds to 500 milliseconds.
- **Rationale:** Constrains the static schedule (SW-REQ-SYS-010) to cover all FT1 app rates: IMU 200 Hz (SYS-005), altimeter 20 Hz (SYS-008), GPS 5 Hz (SYS-009), nav 100 Hz (SYS-012), and telemetry 2 Hz (SYS-019).
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-005** — Deterministic Invocation Order

- **Description:** The SCH library shall invoke applications in a deterministic order on every scheduler cycle.
- **Rationale:** PM-required determinism (SW-REQ-SYS-044) so Trick simulation and flight runs are repeatable.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-006** — Scheduler Continues After Application Failure

- **Description:** The SCH library shall continue invoking other registered applications when one application returns a failure status.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: app failures must not halt the scheduler; other apps continue running per SW-REQ-SYS-062.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-062
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-007** — Application Lifecycle Start Invocation

- **Description:** The SCH library shall invoke each registered application's start hook once before its first periodic invocation.
- **Rationale:** Required so apps initialize internal state once before periodic processing begins per LibJuno app lifecycle.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-008** — POSIX and Pico2 Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The SCH library shall produce equivalent application invocation sequences on POSIX and Pico2 builds.
- **Rationale:** PM-required POSIX/Pico2 equivalence (SW-REQ-SYS-043) so Trick simulation exercises identical scheduling paths.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-009** — Scheduler Capacity Bounded At Compile Time

- **Description:** The SCH library shall enforce a compile-time bound on the number of registered applications.
- **Rationale:** PM constraint: no dynamic memory allocation; capacity must be a compile-time constant per SW-REQ-SYS-050.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-010** — Caller-Owned Scheduler Storage

- **Description:** The SCH library shall use only caller-provided storage and shall not allocate memory dynamically.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR (SW-REQ-SYS-050): no dynamic allocation after boot; all storage caller-owned per LibJuno pattern.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-050
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-TC-SCH-001** — Register Application With Fixed Period

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SCH-001
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active

- **Acceptance Criteria:** JunoSch_RegisterApp returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, the registered app count increments by one, and the stored period equals 10 ms.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Call JunoSch_RegisterApp() with the scheduler root, the mock application, and period=10 ms.
  2. Capture the returned status code.
  3. Query the scheduler for the registered application count.
  4. Inspect the registered period associated with the mock application.

- **Acceptance Criteria:** All three registrations return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and the stored periods match 5 ms, 50 ms, and 500 ms respectively.
- **Procedure:**

  3. Read the FAST and SLOW counters.

## Details
### **SW-REQ-SD-001** — SD Card Initialization at Startup

- **Description:** The SD library shall initialize the SD card during power-on self-test.
- **Rationale:** FT1 POST must probe the SD card so the operator knows pre-flight whether logging storage is available.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-029
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-002** — SD Card Capacity Reporting

- **Description:** The SD library shall report the SD card capacity after successful initialization.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: capacity is observable at POST so the operator can confirm sufficient storage exists pre-flight.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-029
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-003** — Run Directory Creation Per Power-On

- **Description:** The SD library shall create a new run directory on each power-on.
- **Rationale:** FT1 requires each power-on to start a fresh log run distinct from prior runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-025
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-004** — Prior Run Preservation

- **Description:** The SD library shall preserve prior run directories without modification or deletion.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: prior flight data is protected against accidental overwrite between runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-055
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-005** — Sequential Byte Write Surface

- **Description:** The SD library shall accept sequential byte writes into a file within the current run directory.
- **Rationale:** FT1 mission log writes raw, nav, and event bytes; the SD library provides the write surface.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-022
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-006** — Format-Agnostic Byte-Through Writes

- **Description:** The SD library shall write caller-supplied bytes verbatim without modification.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: SD library does not define log format; mlog_lib supplies machine-parseable bytes.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-023
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-007** — Sustain Full-Rate Logging Throughput

- **Description:** The SD library shall sustain write throughput sufficient for full-rate FSW sensor and nav logging.
- **Rationale:** FT1 logs sensors at full sample rate plus nav and events; the SD library must keep up without backpressure.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-001
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-008** — Continue Writes After Transient Failure

- **Description:** The SD library shall continue attempting writes after a write failure.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: SD failures must not halt mission; the library retries writes on transient errors.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-035
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-009** — Write Failure Status Reporting

- **Description:** The SD library shall return a failure status on each write that does not complete successfully.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: SD write failures must be observable so the health state can flag the SD card unhealthy.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-060
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-010** — Continuous Health Status

- **Description:** The SD library shall publish a health status reflecting recent write success.
- **Rationale:** PM-required ongoing health observability so the SD bit of the sensor health bitmap stays current.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-031
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-011** — POSIX Build Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The SD library POSIX build shall expose the same write and run-directory behavior as the Pico2 build.
- **Rationale:** PM-required so Trick simulation exercises the same logging paths as flight hardware.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SD-012** — Deterministic Write Behavior

- **Description:** The SD library shall produce identical on-disk bytes given identical inputs.
- **Rationale:** PM-required determinism so Trick sim runs and regression analysis are repeatable.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

- **Acceptance Criteria:** Every byte read from disk matches the corresponding source byte; no insertions, deletions, escaping, or transformations occur.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Generate a 64 KiB buffer containing every byte value 0x00..0xFF repeating, plus embedded 0x00 and 0xFF runs.

  4. Read the file back and compare byte-for-byte against the original buffer.

### **SW-TC-SD-009** — Sustained Logging Throughput on Pico 2 Hardware

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SD-007
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Type:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Pico 2 flashed with FT1 FSW image. Class 10 (or better) SD card inserted. Serial terminal open at 115200 baud. Stopwatch or host logger ready.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** No backpressure or dropped-write warnings appear on serial; sustained throughput meets or exceeds the FT1 full-rate logging budget recorded in the design doc.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Power on the Pico 2 and wait for POST to complete on the serial terminal.
  2. Trigger the throughput demo command (or run the production logging path with all sensors enabled).
  3. Run the system for 120 seconds while it logs full-rate sensor, nav, and event data.
  4. Observe the serial terminal for any backpressure, dropped-write, or queue-full warnings.
  5. Power down the Pico 2, remove the SD card, and read the active run directory on a host PC.
  6. Compute the total bytes written and divide by elapsed run duration to obtain sustained throughput.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - throughput_serial_log.txt (serial_output): Serial terminal capture for the 120 s run showing absence of backpressure warnings.
  - run_dir_byte_count.txt (log): Host-side report of total bytes written, run duration, and computed sustained throughput.
- **Google Test Ref:** None

### **SW-TC-SD-010** — Writes Continue After Injected Transient Failure

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SD-008
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit

- **Setup:** POSIX SD mock that returns a transient write error on the Nth write call and succeeds on subsequent calls. SD library initialized; log file open.

- **Procedure:**
  1. Issue write A (expect success).
  2. Issue write B with the mock primed to return a transient error (expect failure status).
  3. Issue write C with the mock returning success.
  4. Flush and close, then read the file from the image.

- **Google Test Ref:** libs/sd_lib/tests/sd_lib_test.cpp

## Details
### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-001** — Six-DOF Rigid-Body Truth State

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall produce a six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body truth state during each simulation run.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined sim_dynamics scope: provide truth state with three translational and three rotational DOFs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-002** — Truth State Composition

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics truth state shall contain position, velocity, attitude quaternion, and angular velocity.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined truth-state composition required by sim_sensors and sim_scenario consumers.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-003** — NED Position and Velocity Frame

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall express truth position and velocity in the NED frame consistent with the FSW.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: truth frames must match FSW conventions (SYS-040) so sim_scenario can compare directly.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-004** — Body-to-NED Quaternion Attitude

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall express truth attitude as a unit quaternion rotating from body frame to NED.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: truth attitude representation must match FSW convention (SYS-041, SYS-057).
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-005** — Motor Thrust Force

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall apply a time-varying motor thrust force from a configured thrust curve.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined sim_dynamics scope: motor thrust is a primary force input to the EOM.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-006** — Gravitational Acceleration

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall apply a uniform gravitational acceleration to the vehicle truth state.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined sim_dynamics scope: uniform gravity is the second primary force input.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-007** — Aerodynamic Drag Force

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall apply an aerodynamic drag force computed from drag coefficient, reference area, and airspeed.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined sim_dynamics scope: simplified Cd and reference-area drag model is the third force input.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-008** — Configurable Mass and Inertia Properties

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall accept configured vehicle mass and inertia tensor as inputs.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: mass properties are scenario inputs, not hard-coded in dynamics.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-009** — Fixed-Step Time Integration

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall integrate the equations of motion using a fixed-step deterministic integrator.
- **Rationale:** PM-required determinism (SYS-044) and matching the Trick scheduler step rate.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-010** — Deterministic Truth Output

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall produce identical truth-state output given identical configured inputs.
- **Rationale:** PM-required determinism for repeatable Trick sim runs and regression analysis (SYS-044).
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-011** — Truth State Update Cadence

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall publish truth state at every integration step of the Trick scheduler.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: sim_sensors and sim_scenario consume truth state at the scheduler step rate.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-012** — Ground Impact Termination

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall stop integrating motion once the vehicle reaches ground level.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined sim_dynamics scope: ground impact terminates dynamics; truth pinned at impact state.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-013** — Post-Impact Truth State Hold

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall hold the truth-state position and orientation constant after ground impact.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined sim_dynamics scope: post-impact truth state is pinned for downstream consumers.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-014** — SI Units for Truth State

- **Description:** The sim_dynamics module shall express all truth-state quantities in SI units.
- **Rationale:** PM decision (SYS-042): SI units throughout to eliminate unit-conversion ambiguity at the sim boundary.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-003** — Gravity-Only Vertical Free Fall in NED

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-003, SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-006
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Initial state: position [0,0,-100] m (NED, 100 m above ground), velocity zero, attitude identity, no thrust, no drag, gravity 9.81 m/s^2.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Position Down component matches analytical free-fall to within 1e-3 m; velocity Down component matches 9.81 m/s within 1e-3 m/s; North and East components remain zero within 1e-9.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Configure sim_dynamics with gravity-only force model.
  2. Set initial NED position to [0, 0, -100] m and zero velocity.
  3. Integrate forward for t = 1.0 s of simulated time.
  4. Read truth-state position and velocity.
  5. Compare against analytical free-fall: z(t) = -100 + 0.5*9.81*1.0^2 m (NED Down positive), vz(t) = 9.81*1.0 m/s.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-004** — Body-to-NED Quaternion Identity Mapping

- **Verification Method:** Test

  1. Configure sim_dynamics with identity attitude quaternion and zero angular velocity.
  2. Apply a body-frame thrust along body +X axis equal to 10 N for one step.

  4. Verify body +X thrust maps to NED North acceleration (positive North velocity component) given identity attitude.

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-006, SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-009
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Initial state: position [0,0,-500] m NED, velocity [50, 0, -50] m/s NED, identity attitude, no thrust, no drag, gravity 9.81 m/s^2.

  3. Integrate forward for t = 5.0 s of simulated time.
  4. Read truth-state position.
  5. Compare against analytical projectile: x(t) = 50*t, y(t) = 0, z(t) = -500 + (-50)*t + 0.5*9.81*t^2 (NED Down positive).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-008** — Aerodynamic Drag Force Magnitude

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-007
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Vehicle at rest attitude (identity); velocity [100, 0, 0] m/s NED; Cd = 0.5; reference area = 0.01 m^2; air density = 1.225 kg/m^3; gravity and thrust disabled.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Drag force magnitude equals 30.625 N within 1e-3 N; force vector is anti-parallel to velocity (dot product with velocity unit vector equals -1 within 1e-9).
- **Procedure:**
  1. Configure sim_dynamics with drag-only force model and the listed coefficients.
  2. Set vehicle velocity to [100, 0, 0] m/s and read computed drag force.
  3. Compare drag force magnitude against analytical 0.5 * rho * Cd * A * V^2 = 0.5 * 1.225 * 0.5 * 0.01 * 100^2 = 30.625 N.
  4. Verify drag force vector points opposite to velocity (negative North).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-009** — Drag Scales With Velocity Squared

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-007
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Same drag configuration as SW-TC-SIM-DYN-008; gravity and thrust disabled.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** F(100)/F(50) equals 4.0 within 1e-6; F(200)/F(100) equals 4.0 within 1e-6, demonstrating V^2 scaling.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Compute drag force at velocity 50 m/s along North.
  2. Compute drag force at velocity 100 m/s along North.
  3. Compute drag force at velocity 200 m/s along North.
  4. Compute the ratio of force magnitudes: F(100)/F(50) and F(200)/F(100).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-010** — Configured Mass Affects Translational Acceleration

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-008
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Two sim_dynamics instances: one with mass 1.0 kg, one with mass 2.0 kg. Apply identical 10 N body-frame thrust along +X. Disable gravity and drag.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Velocity ratio v_A / v_B equals 2.0 within 1e-9; absolute velocity values match F/m*dt within 1e-9 m/s.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Initialize instance A with mass 1.0 kg and instance B with mass 2.0 kg.
  2. Apply body-frame thrust of 10 N along body +X to both for one fixed step dt.
  3. Read velocity from each instance.
  4. Assert velocity_A = 10/1.0 * dt and velocity_B = 10/2.0 * dt within tolerance.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-011** — Configured Inertia Affects Angular Acceleration

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-008
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Two sim_dynamics instances with diagonal inertia tensors I_A = diag(0.1, 0.1, 0.1) and I_B = diag(0.2, 0.2, 0.2) kg*m^2. Apply identical 1.0 N*m body-frame torque about body +X. Disable gravity, thrust, drag.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Angular-velocity ratio omega_A_x / omega_B_x equals 2.0 within 1e-6; absolute values match torque/inertia*dt within 1e-6 rad/s.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Initialize instance A with I = diag(0.1, 0.1, 0.1) and instance B with I = diag(0.2, 0.2, 0.2).
  2. Apply 1.0 N*m body torque about body X axis to both for one fixed step dt.
  3. Read angular velocity from each instance.
  4. Assert omega_A_x = 1.0/0.1 * dt and omega_B_x = 1.0/0.2 * dt within tolerance.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-012** — Fixed-Step Integrator Step Size

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-009
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Configure sim_dynamics with fixed step dt = 0.01 s. Initial velocity zero, body thrust 1 N along +X with mass 1 kg, gravity and drag disabled.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Inter-step time delta equals configured dt exactly (bit-identical) for all 100 steps; total simulated time equals N*dt within floating-point rounding (1e-12 s).
- **Procedure:**
  1. Step the integrator 100 times.
  2. Record the simulated time after each step.
  3. Verify each successive simulated-time delta equals 0.01 s exactly (no drift).
  4. Verify final simulated time equals 1.0 s within 1e-12 s.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-010
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Two sim_dynamics instances with identical configuration: same mass, inertia, initial state, thrust curve, gravity, drag.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** All truth-state fields (position, velocity, quaternion, angular velocity) at all 1000 steps are bitwise identical between runs A and B.

  1. Run instance A for 1000 fixed steps and record full truth-state trajectory.

  3. Compare each truth-state field at every step between the two trajectories.
  4. Assert exact bitwise equality of all truth-state fields at all steps.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_dynamics/tests/sim_dynamics_test.cpp

- **Verification Method:** Test

### **SW-TC-SIM-DYN-015** — Integration Stops at Ground Impact

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-DYN-012
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit

- **Acceptance Criteria:** After the step at which position Down reaches 0 m, position and velocity values do not change in subsequent steps; the integrator reports that motion has terminated at impact.

- **Type:** Unit

## Details
### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-001** — Trick S_define Integration

- **Description:** The sim harness shall integrate sim_dynamics, sim_sensors, sim_scenario, and FSW POSIX into a single Trick simulation.
- **Rationale:** PM-required Trick top-level integration providing a single closed-loop SITL simulation for FT1 nav anchoring.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-002** — Time-Stepped Sim Orchestration

- **Description:** The sim harness shall advance the simulation on a fixed time step driven by the Trick scheduler.
- **Rationale:** PM-required deterministic time-stepped orchestration so dynamics, sensors, and FSW execute in a repeatable order.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-003** — Sensor-to-FSW Boundary

- **Description:** The sim harness shall deliver simulated sensor measurements to the FSW POSIX driver inputs each step.
- **Rationale:** PM-required boundary between Trick-side sensor models and the FSW POSIX driver layer for each scheduled step.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-004** — POSIX FSW Execution Inside Sim

- **Description:** The sim harness shall execute the FSW POSIX applications and libraries in-process during each simulation step.
- **Rationale:** PM-required so Trick exercises the same FSW software paths used on flight hardware via the POSIX build.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-005** — Scenario Configuration Selection

- **Description:** The sim harness shall select the scenario configuration via Trick command-line arguments at run start.
- **Rationale:** PM-required command-line scenario selection to enable batch runs and operator-driven configuration.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-006** — Reproducible Run Output

- **Description:** The sim harness shall produce identical run outputs given identical scenario configuration and random seed inputs.
- **Rationale:** PM-required reproducibility for regression analysis and FT1 nav anchoring across repeated Trick runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-007** — SD Log Artifact Emission

- **Description:** The sim harness shall emit the FSW SD card log as a file artifact each run.
- **Rationale:** PM-required SD log artifact captured during sim runs for post-run analysis and FT1 anchoring.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-008** — Telemetry Capture Artifact

- **Description:** The sim harness shall capture FSW telemetry packets to a file artifact each run.
- **Rationale:** PM-required telemetry transcript artifact captured during sim runs for ground-station behavioral verification.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-009** — Truth-vs-FSW Comparison Artifact

- **Description:** The sim harness shall write a truth-versus-FSW comparison file containing simulated truth and FSW nav state.
- **Rationale:** PM-required comparison artifact enabling nav-vs-truth post-run analysis for FT1 sim closure.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SIM-HARN-010** — Run Artifact Output Directory

- **Description:** The sim harness shall collect all run output artifacts under a single configurable output directory.
- **Rationale:** PM-required collection of all sim artifacts in one known location for downstream tooling and archival.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-TC-SIM-SCEN-001** — Scenario File Format - Human Editable Inspection

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SCEN-001
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Type:** Integration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Checkout repository at the FT1 baseline tag. Open the scenario file directory under sim/sim_scenario/scenarios/ in a text editor.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Scenario file is plain text, hand-editable, produces a readable diff under git, and edits are picked up by the loader without recompilation.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Open the FT1 baseline scenario file in a plain text editor.
  2. Inspect the file for human-readable structured text (e.g., YAML/JSON/Trick input syntax) without binary content.
  3. Modify a scalar parameter (e.g., launch elevation), save, and re-run the loader to confirm the change is consumed.
  4. Verify the file is tracked in git and produces a readable diff when modified.

- **Rationale:** PM-required ADC quantization match to real IMU so FSW driver layer observes identical resolution behavior.

- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-006** — Configurable IMU Noise and Bias

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall apply configurable white noise and bias to synthetic IMU measurements.
- **Rationale:** PM-required realism so nav-evaluation runs reflect realistic IMU error characteristics; parameters loaded from sim_scenario.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-007** — Synthetic Barometer Sample Rate

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall produce synthetic barometer measurements at 20 Hz.
- **Rationale:** PM-required match to SW-REQ-SYS-008 so FSW POSIX drivers consume sim baro at the same cadence as real baro.

### **SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-008** — Standard Atmosphere Pressure and Temperature

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall derive synthetic pressure and temperature from truth altitude using a standard atmosphere model.
- **Rationale:** PM-required physically consistent baro outputs anchored to truth altitude for closed-loop nav evaluation.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-045
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-009** — Configurable Barometer Noise

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall apply configurable noise to synthetic barometer measurements.
- **Rationale:** PM-required realism so nav baro fusion is exercised under realistic noise; parameters loaded from sim_scenario.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft

- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, sim

### **SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-010** — Synthetic GPS Sample Rate

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall produce synthetic GPS position fixes at 5 Hz.

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall apply configurable HDOP, VDOP, fix latency, and satellite count to synthetic GPS fixes.

- **Description:** The sim_sensors module shall suppress synthetic GPS fixes during configured dropout windows.

## Details
### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-001** — Synthetic Sensor Generation From Truth State

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-001
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with a deterministic sim_dynamics truth state providing fixed position, velocity, attitude, angular rate, and specific force.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** All three sensor outputs (IMU, baro, GPS) are populated and match the analytical expectations within floating-point tolerance.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Initialize sim_sensors with zero noise, zero bias, and zero dropout configuration.
  2. Step the model once with a known truth state vector.
  3. Read the synthetic IMU, barometer, and GPS outputs from the model.
  4. Compare each output against the analytically-expected value derived from the truth state.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-002** — Synthetic IMU Sample Rate Is 200 Hz

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-002
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors and run for one simulated second with a constant truth state.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Exactly 200 synthetic IMU samples are emitted in 1.0 s and inter-sample period is 5.0 ms within +/-1 sub-step tolerance.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Configure sim_sensors with default parameters and a 1.0 s run duration.
  2. Advance simulated time at the smallest sub-step the model supports.
  3. Count the number of distinct synthetic IMU samples emitted during the run.
  4. Record timestamps of consecutive IMU samples.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-003** — Synthetic Accelerometer Saturates At Plus Or Minus 16 G

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-003
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with zero noise and zero bias.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Accelerometer outputs are clamped to +16 G for positive overrange inputs and -16 G for negative overrange inputs on all three axes.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Drive truth specific force on the X axis to +50 G and step the model.
  2. Read the synthetic accelerometer X output and record it.
  3. Drive truth specific force on the X axis to -50 G and step the model.
  4. Read the synthetic accelerometer X output and record it.
  5. Repeat for the Y and Z axes.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-004** — Synthetic Gyroscope Saturates At Plus Or Minus 2000 dps

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-004
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with zero noise and zero bias.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Gyroscope outputs are clamped to +2000 dps for positive overrange inputs and -2000 dps for negative overrange inputs on all three axes.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Drive truth angular rate on the X axis to +5000 dps and step the model.
  2. Read the synthetic gyroscope X output and record it.
  3. Drive truth angular rate on the X axis to -5000 dps and step the model.
  4. Read the synthetic gyroscope X output and record it.
  5. Repeat for the Y and Z axes.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-005** — Synthetic IMU 16-bit Quantization Resolution

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-005
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with zero noise and zero bias and configured full-scale ranges of +/-16 G and +/-2000 dps.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Emitted IMU counts span the signed 16-bit range, increment monotonically with input, and match the configured LSB scaling within one count.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Sweep truth specific force across the full +/-16 G range in fine steps and record raw counts emitted.
  2. Sweep truth angular rate across the full +/-2000 dps range in fine steps and record raw counts emitted.
  3. Verify emitted counts are signed 16-bit integers.
  4. Verify the count delta per LSB matches the configured full-scale divided by 32768.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-006** — Configurable IMU White Noise Statistics

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-006
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with zero bias, a constant zero-input truth state, and a configured noise standard deviation sigma_a for accelerometer and sigma_g for gyroscope.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Per-axis sample mean is zero within 3*sigma/sqrt(N), and sample standard deviation matches configured sigma within 5 percent.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Run the model for at least 10000 IMU samples with the configured noise parameters.
  2. Collect the synthetic accelerometer and gyroscope sample streams per axis.
  3. Compute the sample mean and sample standard deviation per axis.
  4. Compare results against the configured sigma values.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-007** — Configurable IMU Bias Offsets Mean Output

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-006
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with zero noise and a configured non-zero bias vector for accelerometer and gyroscope.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Per-axis sample mean equals the configured bias for both accelerometer and gyroscope within floating-point tolerance.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Hold truth specific force and angular rate at zero.
  2. Step the model for at least 1000 IMU samples.
  3. Compute the per-axis sample mean of accelerometer and gyroscope outputs.
  4. Compare the per-axis means against the configured bias values.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** sim/sim_sensors/tests/sim_sensors_test.cpp

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-008
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit

### **SW-TC-SIM-SENS-010** — Configurable Barometer Noise Statistics

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SIM-SENS-009
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sim_sensors with constant truth altitude and configured baro noise standard deviation sigma_p.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Residual mean is zero within 3*sigma/sqrt(N), and residual standard deviation matches configured sigma_p within 5 percent.

  1. Run the model for at least 5000 barometer samples.

  3. Compute sample mean and sample standard deviation of the residual stream.
  4. Compare against the configured sigma_p.

- **Verification Method:** Test

- **Acceptance Criteria:** Zero GPS fixes are emitted during [2,4] s, and fixes resume at the configured 5 Hz cadence in (4,6].
