## Details
### **SW-REQ-SYS-001** — Raw Sensor Logging to SD Card

- **Description:** The FSW shall log all raw sensor measurements to the SD card during the mission.
- **Rationale:** FT1 mission role requires preservation of raw sensor data for post-flight analysis and Trick simulation anchoring.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-002** — Live In-Flight Navigation Estimation

- **Description:** The FSW shall execute a live navigation algorithm in flight to estimate and propagate nav state.
- **Rationale:** FT1 is a nav-evaluation flight; the navigation algorithm must run on flight hardware in real time.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-003** — Live Telemetry Downlink Over LoRa

- **Description:** The FSW shall transmit live telemetry over the LoRa radio during the mission.
- **Rationale:** FT1 requires real-time ground visibility into vehicle state and recovery beaconing post-landing.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-004** — No Actuation on FT1

- **Description:** The FSW shall not command any vehicle actuator during the FT1 mission.
- **Rationale:** FT1 scope is nav evaluation and sim anchoring; actuation is explicitly out of scope.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-005** — IMU Sample Rate

- **Description:** The FSW shall sample the IMU at 200 Hz throughout the mission.
- **Rationale:** PM-fixed IMU rate to bound boost-phase motion (~13 G, 500 ms) and support nav at 100 Hz.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-006** — IMU Accelerometer Range

- **Description:** The FSW shall configure the IMU accelerometer range to plus or minus 16 G.
- **Rationale:** Flight envelope reaches 13 G; 16 G range provides margin without saturation during boost.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-007** — IMU Gyroscope Range

- **Description:** The FSW shall configure the IMU gyroscope range to plus or minus 2000 degrees per second.
- **Rationale:** Maximum rotation rate envelope for FT1; 2000 dps avoids saturation during boost and recovery.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-008** — Altimeter Sample Rate

- **Description:** The FSW shall sample the barometric altimeter at 20 Hz throughout the mission.
- **Rationale:** PM-fixed rate sufficient for apogee detection (~600 m) and nav baro fusion at 20 Hz cadence.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-009** — GPS Sample Rate

- **Description:** The FSW shall sample the GPS receiver at 5 Hz throughout the mission.
- **Rationale:** PM-fixed GPS rate matches FGPMMOPA6H capability and supports horizontal nav bounding.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-010** — Static Compile-Time Schedule

- **Description:** The FSW shall execute all applications on a static schedule fixed at compile time.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: no dynamic rate changes; deterministic TDM scheduling for repeatable nav and logging.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-011** — No Sensor Downsampling for Logging

- **Description:** The FSW shall log each sensor at its full sample rate without downsampling.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: preserve raw fidelity for post-flight analysis and Trick sim anchoring.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-012** — Nav State Output Rate

- **Description:** The FSW shall publish navigation state estimates at 100 Hz during the mission.
- **Rationale:** PM-fixed nav output cadence supports telemetry, AFM, and consistent post-flight analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-013** — Sixteen-State Navigation Estimate

- **Description:** The FSW shall produce a navigation estimate containing position, velocity, attitude quaternion, and accelerometer and gyroscope biases.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined nav state composition: 3 position, 3 velocity, 4 quaternion, 3 accel bias, 3 gyro bias.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-014** — Navigation Position Bound to GPS

- **Description:** The FSW shall keep the navigation position estimate within a configured horizontal distance of the GPS fix.
- **Rationale:** PM-required black-box divergence sanity bound; numeric threshold lives in design, not requirement.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-015** — Navigation Validity Flag

- **Description:** The FSW shall publish a navigation validity flag indicating whether the nav estimate is currently trustworthy.
- **Rationale:** PM-required observable state so consumers (telemetry, post-flight) can gate use of nav output.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-016** — Automatic Flight Phase Detection

- **Description:** The FSW shall automatically detect boost, apogee, descent, and landing transitions from pre-launch initial phase.
- **Rationale:** PM-required AFM capability; pre-launch is the at-power-on initial phase per SW-REQ-AFM-002; algorithm choice deferred to design.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-017** — Flight Phase Published to Software Bus

- **Description:** The FSW shall publish the current flight phase on the software bus.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: phase is an observable consumed by telemetry and logging via the bus.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-018** — Flight Phase Transition Timestamp Accuracy

- **Description:** The FSW shall timestamp each flight phase transition within one second of post-flight ground-truth determination.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined AFM acceptance tolerance for FT1 closure based on log analysis ground truth.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-019** — Telemetry Downlink Rate

- **Description:** The FSW shall transmit telemetry packets over the LoRa radio at 2 Hz.
- **Rationale:** PM-fixed telemetry rate balancing LoRa link budget against ground-station observability.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-020** — Telemetry Packet Content

- **Description:** The FSW telemetry packet shall include timestamp, phase, GPS fix, baro altitude, nav state, voltage, validity, and health.
- **Rationale:** PM-specified packet content covering mission state required for ground monitoring and recovery.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-021** — Continuous Telemetry Coverage

- **Description:** The FSW shall transmit telemetry continuously from power-on until external power is removed.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: continuous coverage including post-landing recovery beaconing.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-022** — SD Card Log Content

- **Description:** The FSW shall log all raw sensor samples, navigation state, and flight phase events to the SD card.
- **Rationale:** PM-specified log content enabling post-flight analysis and Trick sim anchoring.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-023** — Machine-Parseable Log Format

- **Description:** The FSW shall write SD card log records in a machine-parseable format.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: format details deferred to design but parseability is a requirement.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-024** — Verbatim Raw NMEA Logging

- **Description:** The FSW shall log raw GPS NMEA sentences verbatim to the SD card.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: preserve unmodified GPS source data for post-flight reconstruction.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-025** — New Log Run Per Power-On

- **Description:** The FSW shall create a new log run on each power-on.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: each power-on starts a fresh log run distinct from prior runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-026** — Monotonic Microsecond Time Base

- **Description:** The FSW shall stamp every record using monotonic microseconds since startup as the single time base.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: one canonical time source across all records ensures cross-record alignment.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-027** — Per-Sample Timestamping

- **Description:** The FSW shall include a timestamp on every individual sensor sample record, not only batch headers.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: per-sample timestamps required for accurate post-flight nav reconstruction.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-028** — GPS UTC Time Logging

- **Description:** The FSW shall log a GPS UTC time record whenever the GPS receiver provides UTC time.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: enables post-flight alignment of monotonic time to absolute UTC.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-029** — Power-On Self-Test

- **Description:** The FSW shall execute a power-on self-test probing each sensor device once at startup.
- **Rationale:** PM-required POST so the operator knows pre-flight whether all sensors are responsive.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-030** — POST Result Logging

- **Description:** The FSW shall log the per-sensor POST pass-or-fail result to the SD card once at startup.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: POST result is a one-shot record persisted on the SD card.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-031** — Continuous Sensor Health Bitmap

- **Description:** The FSW shall publish a per-sensor health bitmap continuously throughout the mission.
- **Rationale:** PM-required ongoing health observability included in every telemetry packet and log.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-032** — Operator Health Indicator LED

- **Description:** The FSW shall drive a physical LED reflecting all-healthy versus error state for the operator.
- **Rationale:** PM-required pre-flight visual go/no-go indication for the operator on the pad.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-033** — Sensor Read Failure Continuation

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue operating when a sensor read fails.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: never halt mission on sensor failure; continue execution.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-034** — Navigation Degraded-Input Continuation

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue propagating navigation with reduced inputs when sensor inputs are unavailable.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: nav must never crash; degrade gracefully when sensors drop.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-035** — SD Write Failure Continuation

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue attempting SD card writes after a write failure.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: SD failures must not halt mission; retry writes.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-036** — Radio Failure Continuation

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue all other operations after a telemetry transmission failure.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: radio loss must not impair logging or nav.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-037** — No Auto-Reboot During Mission

- **Description:** The FSW shall not autonomously reboot or reset itself during the mission.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: failures flag and continue; FIDR is out of scope for FT1.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-038** — Geodetic Position Frame

- **Description:** The FSW shall represent position as WGS-84 geodetic latitude and longitude in degrees with altitude in meters.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined coordinate convention for FT1 telemetry, logging, and nav output.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-039** — Height-Above-Ellipsoid Altitude Reference

- **Description:** The FSW shall reference reported altitudes to the WGS-84 ellipsoid (HAE).
- **Rationale:** PM decision: HAE chosen as the unambiguous reference shared with GPS output.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-040** — NED Velocity Frame

- **Description:** The FSW shall express velocity in the North-East-Down (NED) frame.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined aerospace-standard velocity frame for FT1 nav and telemetry.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-041** — Body-to-NED Quaternion Attitude

- **Description:** The FSW shall represent attitude as a unit quaternion (w, x, y, z) rotating from body frame to NED.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined attitude representation for FT1 nav output and telemetry consumers.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-042** — SI Units Throughout

- **Description:** The FSW shall use SI units for all logged and downlinked physical quantities.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: globally SI to eliminate unit-conversion ambiguity.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-043** — POSIX Build Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The FSW POSIX build shall be functionally equivalent to the Pico2 flight build.
- **Rationale:** PM-required so Trick simulation exercises the same software paths as flight.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-044** — Deterministic Execution

- **Description:** The FSW shall produce deterministic outputs given identical inputs.
- **Rationale:** PM-required determinism for repeatable Trick sim runs and regression analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-045** — Trick Simulation Integration

- **Description:** The FSW shall be runnable inside a NASA Trick simulation accepting simulated IMU, baro, and GPS inputs.
- **Rationale:** PM-required closed-loop SITL capability anchored to FT1 sensor suite.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-046** — Operational on Power-On Without Arming

- **Description:** The FSW shall become fully operational immediately at power-on without any external arm signal.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: no arming step; power-on equals mission start.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-047** — Run Until External Power Removed

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue executing until external power is removed, never initiating its own shutdown.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: no FSW-initiated shutdown; operator controls end of mission via power.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-048** — Post-Landing Recovery Beacon

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue transmitting 2 Hz telemetry indefinitely after landing until power is removed.
- **Rationale:** PM-required recovery beaconing supports locating the rocket after landing.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-049** — FT1 Flight Verification Artifacts

- **Description:** The FSW FT1 verification shall produce SD log, telemetry transcript, operator video, signed checklist, and recovered hardware.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined required closure artifacts for FT1 flight-side requirements.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-050** — No Dynamic Memory Allocation After Boot

- **Description:** The FSW shall not perform dynamic memory allocation after boot completes.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR: heap is forbidden post-boot to ensure deterministic memory behavior.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, FT2

### **SW-REQ-SYS-051** — No Runtime Polymorphism After Init

- **Description:** The FSW shall not employ runtime polymorphism after initialization completes.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR: dynamic polymorphism only permitted during initialization for vtable wiring.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, FT2

### **SW-REQ-SYS-052** — No RTTI

- **Description:** The FSW shall be built without runtime type information.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR: RTTI is prohibited; enforced via -fno-rtti compiler flag.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, FT2

### **SW-REQ-SYS-053** — No Thrown Exceptions

- **Description:** The FSW shall not throw C++ exceptions.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR: exceptions are prohibited; enforced via -fno-exceptions compiler flag.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, FT2

### **SW-REQ-SYS-054** — Unit Test Line Coverage

- **Description:** The FSW unit test suite shall achieve 100 percent line coverage.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR: 100% line coverage mandated; no branch coverage requirement applies.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1, FT2

### **SW-REQ-SYS-055** — Prior Log Run Preservation

- **Description:** The FSW shall preserve prior log runs on the SD card until externally wiped.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: protect prior flight data against accidental overwrite between runs.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-056** — POST Result Downlink

- **Description:** The FSW shall downlink the per-sensor POST pass-or-fail result over the radio once at startup.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: POST result is a one-shot record visible on the ground station at startup.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-057** — Body Axes Convention

- **Description:** The FSW shall define body axes as X-forward, Y-right, and Z-down.
- **Rationale:** PM-defined aerospace-standard body axis convention for FT1 nav and telemetry.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-058** — Mark Sensor Unhealthy on Read Failure

- **Description:** The FSW shall mark a sensor unhealthy when a read from that sensor fails.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: failed sensors are flagged unhealthy in the published health state.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-059** — Navigation Validity False on Missing Inputs

- **Description:** The FSW shall set the navigation validity flag false when required nav inputs are unavailable.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: validity flag must reflect degraded input state so consumers gate use.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-060** — Flag SD Card Unhealthy on Write Failure

- **Description:** The FSW shall flag the SD card unhealthy when an SD card write fails.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: SD write failures are surfaced via the published health state.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-061** — Flag Radio Unhealthy on Transmission Failure

- **Description:** The FSW shall flag the radio unhealthy when a telemetry transmission fails.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: radio transmission failures are surfaced via the published health state.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-062** — AFM-Loss Tolerance

- **Description:** The FSW shall continue executing applications at their static rates when flight phase detection is unavailable.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: loss of AFM does not halt the mission; apps run at static rates regardless.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** None
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

## Details
### **SW-TC-SYS-001** — Raw Sensor Logging to SD Card

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-001
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Integration
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** POSIX build with mock IMU, baro, and GPS sensors injected; mock SD card backend.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Log contains every raw IMU, baro, and GPS sample produced by the mocks with no missing records.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Start FSW with mock sensors producing deterministic samples for 5 simulated seconds.
  2. Stop the run and read the resulting SD log file.
  3. Parse log records and confirm IMU, baro, and GPS raw sample records are all present.
  4. Cross-check sample counts in the log against the number of samples produced by each mock.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** apps/sys_app/tests/sys_app_logging_test.cpp

## Details
### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-001** — Execute Power-On Self-Test at Startup

- **Description:** The system app shall execute a power-on self-test probing each sensor device once during startup.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-029: SYS-APP is the composition-root owner that orchestrates the one-shot POST sequence at boot.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-029
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-002** — Record Per-Sensor POST Pass-Or-Fail Result

- **Description:** The system app shall record a per-sensor pass-or-fail result from the power-on self-test.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-029: per-sensor POST outcomes are produced by SYS-APP for downstream logging and downlink consumers.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-029
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-003** — Log POST Result to SD Card

- **Description:** The system app shall log the per-sensor POST result to the SD card once at startup.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-030: SYS-APP is the producer that submits the one-shot POST record to the SD logging path.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-030
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-004** — Downlink POST Result Over Radio

- **Description:** The system app shall publish the per-sensor POST result for telemetry downlink once at startup.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-056: SYS-APP produces the POST result that the telemetry app downlinks at startup.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-056
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-005** — Aggregate Sensor Health Into Bitmap

- **Description:** The system app shall aggregate per-sensor health reports from sensor apps into a single health bitmap.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-031: SYS-APP is the central aggregator that combines per-sensor health states for system-wide observability.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-031
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-006** — Publish Health Bitmap on Software Bus

- **Description:** The system app shall publish the aggregated health bitmap on the software bus continuously throughout the mission.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-031: the bitmap must be available on the bus so telem_app can embed it in every packet.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-031
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-007** — Drive Operator LED Solid Green When All Healthy

- **Description:** The system app shall drive the operator LED solid green when all sensors report healthy.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-032: SYS-APP owns the LED output and uses the all-healthy aggregate to drive the go indication.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-032
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-008** — Drive Operator LED Error Pattern on Unhealthy

- **Description:** The system app shall drive the operator LED with an error pattern when any sensor reports unhealthy.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-032: SYS-APP signals no-go to the operator on the pad whenever the aggregate health is degraded.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-032
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-009** — No Autonomous Reboot During Mission

- **Description:** The system app shall not autonomously reboot or reset the flight software during the mission.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-037: as the lifecycle owner SYS-APP is the only component that could trigger a reboot and must not.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-037
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-010** — Operational Immediately at Power-On

- **Description:** The system app shall complete startup and begin scheduled execution without waiting for any external arm signal.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-046: SYS-APP as composition root must finish wiring and hand off to the scheduler with no arming gate.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-046
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-011** — Run Until External Power Removed

- **Description:** The system app shall continue running and never initiate its own shutdown until external power is removed.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-047: SYS-APP owns the lifecycle and must keep the FSW alive until the operator cuts power.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-047
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SYS-APP-012** — POSIX Build Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The system app POSIX build shall provide the same observable behavior as the Pico2 flight build.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SYS-043: SYS-APP must exercise identical lifecycle and POST flows under Trick simulation as on flight hardware.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-001** — POST Sequence Probes Each Sensor Once at Startup

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-001
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sys_app with mock sensor probe callbacks for each registered sensor (GPS, IMU, etc.). Counters track invocation counts.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Each registered sensor probe is invoked exactly once during startup and is not invoked again on subsequent scheduler ticks.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Construct sys_app and invoke its startup entry point.
  2. Allow the startup phase to complete.
  3. Inspect the per-sensor probe invocation counters.
  4. Drive a second scheduler tick after startup completes.
  5. Re-inspect probe invocation counters.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** apps/sys_app/tests/sys_app_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-002** — POST Records Pass Result for Healthy Sensor

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-002
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Configure sys_app with mock sensor probes that all return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Every sensor entry in the POST result records a Pass status when its probe succeeded.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Run sys_app startup which executes POST.
  2. Read the per-sensor POST result structure exposed by sys_app.
  3. Inspect the pass/fail field for each sensor entry.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None

- **Setup:** Configure sys_app where one mock sensor probe returns a failure status and the rest return success.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** The failing sensor entry records Fail; all other sensor entries record Pass.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Run sys_app startup which executes POST.
  2. Read the per-sensor POST result structure.
  3. Inspect the pass/fail field for the failing sensor and the others.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** apps/sys_app/tests/sys_app_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-004** — POST Result Submitted to SD Logger Once at Startup

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-003
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Wire sys_app to a mock SD logging sink that records each submitted POST log record.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Exactly one POST record is submitted to the SD logger at startup, its per-sensor fields match the mock outcomes, and no further POST records are submitted on later ticks.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Run sys_app startup with a mix of pass and fail mock sensor results.
  2. Verify the mock SD sink received exactly one POST record.
  3. Inspect the recorded payload's per-sensor fields against the configured mock outcomes.
  4. Drive several additional scheduler ticks.
  5. Verify the SD sink received no further POST records.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None

- **Setup:** Initialize sys_app and a mock software bus subscriber subscribed to the POST result topic.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Exactly one POST result message is published on the telemetry downlink topic at startup with per-sensor fields matching the mock outcomes.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Run sys_app startup with mock sensor probe outcomes.
  2. Capture all messages received by the POST topic subscriber during startup.
  3. Inspect the captured POST message's per-sensor fields.
  4. Drive several additional scheduler ticks.
  5. Verify no further POST messages were published.

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-006** — Health Bitmap Aggregates Per-Sensor Reports

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-005
- **Verification Method:** Test

- **Acceptance Criteria:** The aggregated bitmap matches the expected bit pattern for each injected combination of per-sensor health reports.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Inject a healthy report from sensor 0 and unhealthy reports from the rest.
  2. Tick sys_app to consume the reports and update the bitmap.
  3. Read the aggregated bitmap.
  4. Repeat with a different combination of healthy/unhealthy sensors.
  5. Tick and re-read the bitmap.

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-007** — Health Bitmap Published Continuously on Software Bus

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-006
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Integration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Initialize sys_app and a mock software bus subscriber on the health bitmap topic.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Health bitmap messages are published on every scheduled cycle past startup, and the latest published value reflects the current aggregate.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Run sys_app startup.
  2. Drive at least 100 scheduler ticks past startup with stable mock sensor health.
  3. Count the number of health bitmap messages received by the subscriber.
  4. Change the per-sensor mock health reports and drive 100 more ticks.
  5. Verify the latest published bitmap matches the new aggregate.

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-008** — Operator LED Solid Green When All Sensors Healthy

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-007
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Type:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Assemble flight avionics with the operator LED installed. Connect all sensors with valid hardware and antennas/test stimulus so that each sensor reports healthy. Open serial terminal at 115200 baud. Camera ready.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** The operator LED is solid (non-blinking) green for the entire 30-second observation window while the published health bitmap reports all sensors healthy.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Power on the avionics with all sensors connected and functional.
  2. Wait for sys_app POST to complete and the steady-state cadence to begin.
  3. Observe the operator LED for at least 30 seconds.
  4. Photograph the LED in its steady state.
  5. Capture the serial terminal log showing the published health bitmap with all bits asserted healthy.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - led_green_photo.jpg (photo): Photograph of operator LED illuminated solid green during the all-healthy state
  - led_green_video.mp4 (video): Video of LED steady (non-blinking) for at least 30 seconds
  - health_bitmap_log.txt (log): Serial log capturing health bitmap messages with all sensors healthy
- **Google Test Ref:** None

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-009** — Operator LED Error Pattern When Any Sensor Unhealthy

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-008
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Type:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Assemble flight avionics with the operator LED installed. Connect all sensors except one (e.g., disconnect the GPS module) so that at least one sensor reports unhealthy. Open serial terminal at 115200 baud. Camera ready.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** While the sensor is disconnected the LED shows a clearly distinguishable error pattern (not solid green) and the health bitmap reports the affected sensor unhealthy; reconnecting restores solid green within 10 seconds.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Power on the avionics with one sensor intentionally disconnected.
  2. Wait for sys_app POST to complete and the steady-state cadence to begin.
  3. Observe the operator LED for at least 30 seconds.
  4. Photograph and video the LED.
  5. Capture the serial terminal log showing the published health bitmap with the disconnected sensor's bit unhealthy.
  6. Reconnect the sensor and observe that the LED transitions to solid green within 10 seconds.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - led_error_video.mp4 (video): Video of operator LED in error pattern while sensor unhealthy and recovery to green
  - health_bitmap_unhealthy_log.txt (log): Serial log capturing health bitmap messages with affected sensor's bit unhealthy
- **Google Test Ref:** None

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-010** — No Reboot or Reset Calls in sys_app Source

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-009
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Type:** Integration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Static inspection of the sys_app source tree under apps/sys_app/.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** The inspection finds no call sites in sys_app that would autonomously reboot, reset, or terminate the flight software during the mission.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Search apps/sys_app/ for invocations of reboot, watchdog reset, system reset, or equivalent SDK reset entry points.
  2. Search for calls to abort(), exit(), or any function that terminates the program.
  3. Search for writes to RP2350 reset/watchdog registers or LibJuno reset APIs.
  4. Record findings in the inspection log.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** apps/sys_app/tests/sys_app_test.cpp

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-010
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Instantiate sys_app with mock sensors and a flag indicating whether any external arm input was queried during startup.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Startup completes successfully and scheduled execution begins without any external arm signal being queried or asserted.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Invoke sys_app's startup entry point with no arm signal asserted on any input.
  2. Verify startup returns success and that the scheduler has been handed off to.
  3. Inspect the arm-input query flag.
  4. Drive several scheduled ticks and verify they execute normally.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** apps/sys_app/tests/sys_app_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-012** — Power-On to Operational Demonstration

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-010
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Type:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Assemble flight avionics on bench with no external arm jumper, switch, or signal connected. Serial terminal open at 115200 baud and logging to file. Stopwatch ready.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Periodic telemetry messages appear on the serial terminal within a deterministic startup window with no operator action other than applying power.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Start the stopwatch and apply external power to the avionics.
  2. Observe the serial terminal for the sys_app startup banner and POST completion message.
  3. Observe subsequent published telemetry on the serial terminal indicating scheduled execution.
  4. Stop the stopwatch when periodic telemetry is observed.
  5. Save the serial log.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - power_on_serial_log.txt (log): Serial log from power-on through startup banner, POST, and steady-state telemetry
- **Google Test Ref:** None

### **SW-TC-SYS-APP-013** — Run Until External Power Removed

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-SYS-APP-011
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Type:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Assemble flight avionics on bench. Serial terminal open at 115200 baud and logging continuously to file. Wall clock or timestamped log available.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Telemetry is emitted continuously for the entire 30-minute window with no gaps and no shutdown banner, and ceases only when external power is removed.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Apply external power and wait for steady-state telemetry on the serial terminal.
  2. Leave the avionics powered and undisturbed for at least 30 minutes while logging serial output.
  3. Periodically confirm that telemetry continues to be emitted with monotonically increasing timestamps.
  4. Remove external power.
  5. Confirm telemetry stops immediately on power removal.
  6. Save the timestamped serial log.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - endurance_serial_log.txt (log): Timestamped serial log covering 30+ minutes of continuous operation through power removal
- **Google Test Ref:** None

- **Verification Method:** Test

- **Setup:** Build sys_app for the POSIX target. Run under the POSIX test harness with mock sensor probes whose pass/fail outcomes match a prerecorded flight-build scenario.

## Details
### **SW-REQ-TELEM-001** — Build Telemetry Packet From Inputs

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall build a telemetry packet from caller-provided input fields on each call.
- **Rationale:** telem_lib is the packet builder consumed by the telemetry app at the SYS-019 2 Hz cadence.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-003
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-002** — Serialize Packet Into Caller Buffer

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall serialize each packet into a caller-provided byte buffer.
- **Rationale:** Caller-owned memory pattern; telem_lib performs no allocation and writes only to injected storage.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-050
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-003** — Packet Content Coverage

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall include timestamp, phase, GPS fix, baro altitude, nav state, voltage, validity, and health.
- **Rationale:** Mirrors SYS-020 packet content so ground monitoring sees full mission state.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-020
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-004** — Bounded Packet Size

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall produce packets whose serialized size does not exceed the configured maximum.
- **Rationale:** RYLR896 LoRa MTU bounds payload size; lora_lib must accept what telem_lib produces.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-003
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-005** — Integrity Field In Packet

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall append an integrity check field covering the packet contents.
- **Rationale:** Ground station decoder must validate packets against corruption over the LoRa link.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-003
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-006** — Phase-Independent Packet Production

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall produce a packet on every call regardless of flight phase.
- **Rationale:** SYS-021 mandates continuous coverage; telem_lib must not gate output on phase state.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-021
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-007** — Embed Sensor Health Bitmap

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall embed the caller-provided sensor health bitmap in each packet.
- **Rationale:** SYS-031 requires continuous health observability via every telemetry packet.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-031
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-008** — Embed Monotonic Microsecond Timestamp

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall embed the caller-provided monotonic microsecond timestamp in each packet.
- **Rationale:** SYS-026 mandates the monotonic time base on every record, including downlinked packets.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-026
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-009** — Deterministic Serialization

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall produce identical byte output for identical input fields.
- **Rationale:** SYS-044 determinism enables Trick regression and ground decoder consistency.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-010** — POSIX And Pico2 Equivalent Output

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall produce identical serialized bytes on POSIX and Pico2 builds for identical inputs.
- **Rationale:** SYS-043 functional equivalence so Trick simulation exercises the flight-side wire format.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-011** — No Radio Or UART I/O

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall not perform any UART or radio input or output operations.
- **Rationale:** Pure encoder scope; transmission belongs to lora_lib, preserving separation of concerns.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-003
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-012** — Embed Navigation Validity Flag

- **Description:** The telemetry library shall embed the caller-provided navigation validity flag in each packet.
- **Rationale:** SYS-020 packet content includes validity so ground consumers can gate use of nav fields.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-020
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-TC-TELEM-001** — Build Packet From Caller-Provided Inputs

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TELEM-002
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Allocate a caller-owned byte buffer surrounded by guard regions filled with a sentinel pattern (0xA5).
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Guard bytes remain 0xA5 (no out-of-bounds writes) and the buffer interior contains the serialized packet.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Pre-fill guard bytes before and after the output buffer with 0xA5.
  2. Invoke the telem_lib build function with the bounded buffer.
  3. Read the guard regions after the call and compare against the sentinel pattern.
  4. Read the buffer interior and verify it has been written.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None

## Details
### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-001** — Scheduled at Two Hertz

- **Description:** The telem_app shall be scheduled to execute at 2 Hz on the static TDM scheduler.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-019: 2 Hz downlink cadence balances LoRa link budget against ground observability.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-019
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-002** — Subscribe to Telemetry Source Messages

- **Description:** The telem_app shall subscribe to GPS, baro, navigation, flight phase, and sensor health messages on the software bus.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-020: packet content requires composition from these sources via the bus.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-020
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-003** — Compose Packet via telem_lib

- **Description:** The telem_app shall invoke telem_lib to compose a telemetry packet from subscribed bus messages.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-020: app delegates packet composition logic to its controller library per MVC.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-020
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-004** — Embed Sensor Health Bitmap

- **Description:** The telem_app shall include the latest published sensor health bitmap in each transmitted packet.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-031: per-sensor health observability is required in every telemetry packet.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-031
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-005** — Transmit via lora_lib

- **Description:** The telem_app shall hand each composed packet to lora_lib for transmission over the LoRa radio.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-003: live telemetry downlink requires app to invoke radio library.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-003
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-006** — Continuous Operation From Power-On

- **Description:** The telem app shall execute every cycle from power-on until external power is removed.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-021: continuous telemetry coverage from power-on until external power removed.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-021
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-007** — Continue After Transmission Failure

- **Description:** The telem_app shall continue executing subsequent cycles after a transmission failure without halting or backing off.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-036: radio loss must not impair operation; no backoff per PM brief.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-036
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-008** — Publish Radio Health Status

- **Description:** The telem_app shall publish a radio health status indicating success or failure of the most recent transmission.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-061: radio transmission failures are surfaced via the published health state.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-061
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-009** — POSIX and Pico2 Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The telem app shall produce identical published telemetry on POSIX and Pico2 builds for identical bus inputs.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-043: POSIX build must be functionally equivalent to the Pico2 flight build for Trick simulation.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-010** — Post-Landing Recovery Beacon

- **Description:** The telem app shall continue transmitting telemetry indefinitely after landing until external power is removed.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-048: post-landing recovery beaconing supports locating the rocket after landing.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-048
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-011** — Deterministic Telemetry Output

- **Description:** The telem app shall produce identical published telemetry given identical bus inputs.
- **Rationale:** Derived from SW-REQ-SYS-044: determinism required for repeatable Trick sim runs and regression analysis.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active

- **Tags:** FT1

- **Acceptance Criteria:** telem_lib compose receives the most recent value for each subscribed source; no earlier message is forwarded when a newer one is available.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Publish two successive GPS messages on the bus before any execute cycle.
  2. Publish two successive baro messages similarly.
  3. Trigger one telem_app execute cycle.
  4. Inspect the inputs the mock telem_lib received and compare each field to the second (latest) published value for that source.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** apps/telem_app/tests/telem_app_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TELEM-APP-013** — Radio Health Published Every Cycle

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TELEM-APP-008
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit

- **Setup:** Wire telem_app to a mock bus that counts radio health publications per cycle and a mock lora_lib returning a steady-state status, and a stubbed telem_lib (radio health publish path follows compose-then-transmit).
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Exactly one radio health status is published per execute cycle in both scenarios, totaling 10 publications per 10 cycles, with status matching the configured outcome.

## Details
### **SW-REQ-TIME-001** — Monotonic Microsecond Time Source

- **Description:** The time library shall provide a monotonic time value expressed in microseconds since FSW startup.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-026; a monotonic microsecond counter is the canonical FSW time base for all records.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-026
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TIME-002** — Non-Decreasing Time Values

- **Description:** The time library shall return time values that never decrease between successive queries.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-026 and SW-REQ-SYS-044; monotonicity is the deterministic property the system depends on.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TIME-003** — Sixty-Four-Bit Counter Width

- **Description:** The time library shall represent the monotonic time value using a 64-bit unsigned integer.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-026; 64-bit width prevents wrap during the FT1 mission and any plausible future mission.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-026
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TIME-004** — Per-Call Time Query Interface

- **Description:** The time library shall provide an interface returning the current monotonic time value on each call.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-027; per-record timestamping requires callers to query time at each sample event.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-027
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TIME-005** — Bounded Query Latency

- **Description:** The time library shall return from a time query without blocking on I/O or scheduling.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-044; cheap and deterministic time queries keep the TDM scheduler loop predictable.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TIME-006** — POSIX Implementation Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The time library shall provide a POSIX implementation functionally equivalent to the Pico2 implementation.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-043; Trick simulation requires POSIX builds that exercise the same time API as flight.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-TIME-007** — Pico2 Implementation for Flight Hardware

- **Description:** The time library shall provide a Pico2 implementation returning monotonic microseconds from the on-board hardware time base.
- **Rationale:** Decomposes SW-REQ-SYS-043; flight hardware build requires a Pico2 implementation paired with the POSIX implementation.
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Active
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

## Details
### **SW-TC-TIME-001** — Monotonic Microsecond Time Source Returns Value

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-001
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Two consecutive Now()/TimestampToMicros samples with a 1 ms sleep between them differ by at least 1000 microseconds.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Initialize tTime via juno::time::TimeInit(tTime, tApi, nullptr, nullptr).
  2. Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) once and derive the microsecond value via tTime.TimestampToMicros(tNow.tOk).tOk.
  3. Sample monotonic time twice with std::this_thread::sleep_for in between; assert second microsecond sample > first sample by at least the sleep duration.
  4. Verify the Now call returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and the derived microsecond value is non-zero after FSW startup has elapsed at least one microsecond.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-002** — Time Values Are Non-Decreasing Across Successive Queries

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-002
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Across 10000+ successive calls, no microsecond value is less than its predecessor, and the final value strictly exceeds the initial value.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Capture an initial microsecond value t0 by calling tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and tTime.TimestampToMicros(tNow.tOk).tOk.
  2. Loop at least 10000 iterations, calling Now and TimestampToMicros on each iteration to obtain ti.
  3. On each iteration assert that ti is greater than or equal to the previous value t(i-1).
  4. After the loop, assert that the final value is strictly greater than t0.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-003** — Time Value Type Width Is 64-Bit Unsigned

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-003
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib and link the Google Test binary with <type_traits> and <cstdint> available.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** The microsecond value derived from TimestampToMicros is 8 bytes wide, unsigned, integral, and equivalent to uint64_t.
- **Procedure:**
  1. In a Google Test, take the microsecond value type returned by tTime.TimestampToMicros(tTs).tOk (the .tOk field of RESULT_T<uint64_t>).
  2. Use static_assert or EXPECT to confirm sizeof(decltype(tOk)) == 8.
  3. Use std::is_unsigned and std::is_integral to confirm the type is an unsigned integral type.
  4. Confirm the type is std::is_same<decltype(tOk), uint64_t>::value == true.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-004** — Per-Call Time Query Returns Updated Values

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-004
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Each successive Now() call returns a freshly sampled, larger microsecond value, demonstrating per-call sampling rather than a cached constant.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and TimestampToMicros to obtain t0_us.
  2. Sleep for at least 1 millisecond using std::this_thread::sleep_for.
  3. Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and TimestampToMicros again to obtain t1_us.
  4. Assert t1_us > t0_us and that (t1_us - t0_us) is at least 1000 microseconds.
  5. Repeat the query a third time after another 1 ms wait and confirm t2_us > t1_us.
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-005** — Time Query Latency Is Bounded And Non-Blocking

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-005
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary on a host capable of std::chrono::steady_clock.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** Average per-call latency over 100000 Now() invocations is below 50 microseconds, demonstrating that the time query does not block on I/O or scheduling.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Record a wall-clock start timestamp using std::chrono::steady_clock.
  2. Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) 100000 times in a tight loop.
  3. Record a wall-clock stop timestamp using std::chrono::steady_clock.
  4. Compute the average per-call duration as (stop - start) / 100000.
  5. Assert that the average per-call duration is less than 50 microseconds (well below any blocking I/O or scheduling cost).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-006** — POSIX Implementation Public API Equivalence

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-006
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib with the POSIX backend selected. The same LibJuno public header (libjuno/include/juno/time/time_api.hpp) used by the Pico2 build must compile and link in the POSIX build.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** All juno::time::TIME_API_T function references are callable through the POSIX backend, return successful status, produce 64-bit monotonic microsecond values via TimestampToMicros, and compile against the unified LibJuno public header shared with the Pico2 build.
- **Procedure:**
  1. In a Google Test compiled against the POSIX backend, include the LibJuno public header juno/time/time_api.hpp.
  2. Call each function reference in juno::time::TIME_API_T (Now, SleepTo, Sleep) through tTime.ptApi and verify each returns a successful status.
  3. Verify the value derived from tTime.TimestampToMicros(tNow.tOk).tOk is a 64-bit unsigned monotonic microsecond value (reuse the type checks from SW-TC-TIME-003).
  4. Confirm the test compiles and links against the same LibJuno header that the Pico2 build uses (no POSIX-only symbols leak into the public API).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-007** — POSIX Time Source Tracks Wall Clock Elapsed Duration

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-006, SW-REQ-TIME-002
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Type:** Unit
- **Status:** Active
- **Setup:** Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** The POSIX implementation reports an elapsed delta within [95000, 200000] microseconds for a 100 ms sleep, demonstrating monotonic microsecond tracking equivalent to flight.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and tTime.TimestampToMicros to obtain t0_us.
  2. Sleep for exactly 100 milliseconds using std::this_thread::sleep_for.
  3. Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and tTime.TimestampToMicros to obtain t1_us.
  4. Compute delta_us = t1_us - t0_us.
  5. Assert delta_us is greater than or equal to 95000 and less than or equal to 200000 (allowing for scheduler jitter on the host).
- **Expected Artifacts:** None
- **Google Test Ref:** libs/time_lib/tests/time_test.cpp

### **SW-TC-TIME-008** — Pico2 Implementation Hardware Demonstration

- **Requirements Verified:** SW-REQ-TIME-007
- **Verification Method:** Demonstration
- **Type:** Demonstration
- **Status:** Draft
- **Setup:** Flash a demo firmware onto the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 that prints time_lib microsecond values (via tTime.ptApi->Now and tTime.TimestampToMicros) over USB serial at 1 Hz for at least 30 seconds. Open a host serial terminal at 115200 baud and capture the output to a log file.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** The Pico2 firmware prints a monotonically increasing 64-bit microsecond stream for at least 30 seconds, with the first-to-last delta matching the elapsed wall-clock duration within 5 percent.
- **Procedure:**
  1. Connect the Pico2 board to the host via USB.
  2. Flash the time-demo firmware onto the Pico2.
  3. Open the serial terminal at 115200 baud and begin logging to time_demo_serial.log.
  4. Reset the Pico2 and let the firmware run for at least 30 seconds.
  5. Stop logging and inspect time_demo_serial.log.
  6. Verify each printed value is a 64-bit unsigned microsecond count and that successive values are strictly increasing.
  7. Verify the difference between the first and last printed value approximates the elapsed wall-clock time within 5 percent.
- **Expected Artifacts:**
  - time_demo_serial.log (log): USB-serial capture of Pico2 firmware printing time_lib microsecond values at 1 Hz for at least 30 seconds.
- **Google Test Ref:** None
